# Hobby pages

"Things to try" is the hobbies section: seven hobbies Truman actually does, each a page with a small interactive toy (an "island") and something personal from his own records. Every hobby is one JSON file in `src/content/hobbies/<slug>.json`, a card with a stipple plate, an opening scene when the card is clicked, and the page `src/pages/hobbies/[slug].astro`, which renders the header, the island, the personal element and any gallery.

| Hobby              | Island                                                                                 | Data                                                            | Personal element                                                         |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `aquarium-keeping` | `AquariumTank.astro`; `aquarium.ts`, `aquarium-jump.ts`, `stocking.ts`                 | `aquarium-species.ts`                                           | the video of his tank (`video`, `HobbyVideo.astro`) and his tank gallery (`media`) |
| `tide-pooling`     | `TidePool.astro` + `FieldJournal` + `SpecimenCard`; `tidepool.ts`                      | `tidepool-species.ts`, `tidepool-photos.json`                   | his iNaturalist observations (`INatObservations.astro`)                  |
| `fishing`          | `Fishing.astro`; `fishing.ts`, `fishing-sprites.ts`                                    | `fishing-waters.json`, `fishing-species.ts`, `fishing-geo.json` | his catches (`fishing-catches.json`)                                     |
| `birding`          | `Birding.astro`; `birding.ts` (MediaPipe, on device), `birding-bird.ts`, `bird-ink.ts` | `public/birding/face_landmarker.task`                           | spark bird and life list (`BirdingSpark.astro`, `BirdingLifeList.astro`) |
| `herping`          | `HerpingNight.astro` + `FieldJournal` + `SpecimenCard`; `herping.ts`                   | `herping-species.ts`, `herping-photos.json`                     | his herp map (`INatHerpMap.astro`, `herp-geo.json`)                      |
| `hiking`           | `PixelHike.astro`; `hiking.ts`, `hiking-model.ts`, `hiking-renderer.ts`                | none                                                            | Trails I've walked: my hikes from the archive, linking to their sessions (`TrailsWalked.astro`, `trails` in `hiking.json`) |
| `narrow-nature`    | `DayList.astro`                                                                        | see the [narrow-nature](../narrow-nature/SKILL.md) skill        | none, it's a puzzle                                                      |

Components are in `src/components/hobbies/`, engines and data in `src/lib/hobbies/`. Shared parts: `SpecimenCard.astro` (the reveal card), `FieldJournal.astro`, `specimen.ts` (`stampFind`, the "New, to your journal" stamp), `pixel-reveal.ts`, `src/lib/motion.ts` (`rollTo`, `setHair`, `stamp`, underline tabs), `src/lib/covered.ts` (`whenUncovered`), `inat-place.ts` (places rounded to 0.1°), `src/lib/canvas-font.ts` (`canvasFont`, `canvasFontReady`: Libre Franklin for any text a canvas draws), and the `.range` slider in `global.css`. The long reference, one section per hobby, is [docs/hobbies.md](../../../docs/hobbies.md).

Related skills: [stipple-plates](../stipple-plates/SKILL.md) for the card art, [hobby-scenes](../hobby-scenes/SKILL.md) for the click animation, [site-motion](../site-motion/SKILL.md) for stamps, jumps and other motion, [truman-voice](../truman-voice/SKILL.md) and [site-copy](../../instructions/site-copy.instructions.md) for every word on the page.

## Truman's rules for hobbies

- **Every hobby has a personal element** from his own life or records ("look at how i made the other hobbie sections personal", 2026-06-29). Copy isn't a personal element (2026-11-12).
- **Real and accurate.** Species, facts, places and photos must hold up in front of experts: "it has to be completely accurate and also images. that way i can give it to experts and hobbyists" (2026-10-09). Facts are checkable against field guides or Wikipedia, never invented numbers, and doubtful ones get looked up twice.
- **Animals first.** He wants the toys "more animal focused"; plants make dead-end clues. Reveal photos must be "clear and of the animal" (2026-07-08).
- **Real maps.** "make it a real map and make it a heat map of the actual true locations" (2026-07-08), and on a phone it must pinch and zoom (2026-07-09).
- **On device, no per-visitor AI spend.** He turned down a generative model for the selfie bird because "a couple users could spam that and immedaitely eat my credits" (2026-06-28). A selfie never leaves the device, and the page says so.
- **Privacy.** iNaturalist places show a town or region at most, on a 0.1° grid. Hidden fishing spots are never named, in copy, file names or URLs ("just say small river", 2026-10-13). Photographer credits sit in a closed footnote, because a name can give a place away.
- **Nothing covers the animal.** Stamps and badges go beside the photo, never over it ("don't put this directly over the animal image", 2026-10-15). The one exception is Narrow nature's small price stamp in the corner of a large clue photo: "its fine on the photo since the photo is large and this is small and in top right" (2026-10-25).
- **New toys start quiet.** He asked for the first version of the puzzle "not making it too visible yet" (2026-10-08). Ask before putting something new at the top of the section.
- **Daily toys go first.** Narrow nature leads Things to try because "it is most likely to have repeat visitors" (2026-10-13).
- **One at a time.** "start with hobbies shell and just one hobby,. we should build this incrementally not all at once and risk breaking everything" (2026-06-23). Ship one, check it live, then start the next.
- **No upkeep for him.** "I don't want to have to update all of these, uploading the photos is already a lot of work" (2026-06-23). A toy runs on data baked in once or pulled from records he already keeps, like iNaturalist. Never design one around a log he has to fill in.
- Data a hobby shows from iNaturalist is fetched at build time and paged to the end, with the client call as a fallback. No skeleton loaders. (The November 2026 site review, TTT-18 and TTT-19.)
- **Phones from the start.** "ideally these should all work natively on mobile too. the experience doesn't have to be as good as dekstop, but ensure you are developing wiht that in mind" (2026-06-23).
- Clean, "not overly animated slop" (2026-10-14).
- **One look across the section.** A toy may keep its own art colours inside its frame, but everything around and on top of it follows the tokens: no fixed light backgrounds in dark mode, no Tailwind palette colours (#0b1220, #2563eb, #f59e0b, #38bdf8) and no glowing blobs. Text drawn on a canvas uses Libre Franklin 300 or 400 and waits for document.fonts.ready (`canvas-font.ts`; the November 2026 site review, TTT-1 to TTT-4).

## Add a hobby

1. Write `src/content/hobbies/<slug>.json`: `title`, `summary`, `intro`, `plateNote`, `order`, and an `interactive` value and/or a personal block (the schema and JSON glob loader are `hobbies` in `src/content.config.ts`). The intro goes personal history, then what the toy does, then one imperative, in his voice.
2. Plates: add a subject under the same slug in the stipple-plates skill's `subjects.json` (its `note` matches `plateNote`) and render all 12 files into `src/assets/plates/`. `src/lib/plates.test.ts` fails until they all exist. The light `<slug>-card.webp` also becomes the page's link preview, `/og/<slug>.jpg`, at build (`src/pages/og/[slug].jpg.ts`).
3. A new island: add its value to the `interactive` enum in `src/content.config.ts`, put the markup in `src/components/hobbies/<Name>.astro` with a processed `<script>` (never `is:inline`), put the logic in `src/lib/hobbies/<name>.ts` bound through `data-*` hooks, and add a branch in `[slug].astro` inside the `<div class="toy" data-toy={slug}>` wrapper, so the Analytics tab counts who played it ([docs/analytics.md](../../../docs/analytics.md#photos-and-hobbies)). Follow the [island conventions](../../../docs/hobbies.md#interactive-island-conventions): no runtime API calls in the core toy, a keyboard frame with `role="application"`, a `ResizeObserver`, pause when offscreen, a reduced-motion path, and start loops through `whenUncovered()`.
4. Add a case to `src/lib/hobby-facts.ts`, or no facts line shows under the title.
5. Update `src/components/HobbyBand.astro`: a `VERBS` entry for the slug, the `repeat(7, ...)` column count and the band's label.
6. Give it an opening scene (hobby-scenes). Without one, a click falls back to the plain dive or sink.
7. Give it a personal element (below).
8. A new host the browser talks to needs the CSP in `staticwebapp.config.json`, [docs/security.md](../../../docs/security.md#the-csp-unpacked), and the /privacy/ page with its "Last updated" date.
9. Docs: a reference section in docs/hobbies.md, its status line, and the list of islands in the README.

## Give a hobby its personal element

Use one of the blocks that already exist before writing new plumbing: `media` (a gallery), `video` (one of his YouTube uploads in place of the hero photo, with `moments` the toy can link to; [docs/hobbies.md](../../../docs/hobbies.md#a-video-of-the-real-thing)), `inaturalist` (his observations, filtered with `iconicTaxa` or `taxonId`), `lifeList`, `spark`, `herpMap`, `trails` (sessions from his archive as cards that open them; [docs/hobbies.md](../../../docs/hobbies.md#trails-ive-walked-hiking)), or a real-data gallery like the fishing catches. The life list and spark bird come from iNaturalist at build time, with the browser call as a fallback (`birding-inat.ts`). The observations grid and the herp map still fetch near the viewport. All of them fail quietly and round places through `inat-place.ts`. His iNaturalist user id comes from the hobby JSON.

## Species, facts and reveal photos

- Tide pooling and herping: edit `tidepool-species.ts` or `herping-species.ts` (the sprite `category` must already exist; herping also needs `eyeshine`, and `nonNative` where it applies). Two or three facts each, one ID tip and one behaviour fact, one sentence, 8 to 28 words. Run `npx vitest run src/lib/hobbies/species-facts.test.ts`.
- Reveal photos: `npm run fetch:tidepool-photos -- --only <id> --wire inat`, or `npm run fetch:herping-photos -- --place 46 --wire inat` (46 is Washington). Review `staging/<hobby>/photos.json`, then commit the wired JSON.
- Aquarium: the `SPECIES` array in `aquarium-species.ts`. Fishing: `fishing-species.ts`, then the species ids on each water in `fishing-waters.json`. Moving or adding a water needs `node scripts/build-fishing-geo.mjs`, because markers come from `fishing-geo.json`.
- Bird families: `node scripts/fetch-bird-families.mjs`. The life list itself comes from iNaturalist at every build.
- Record a fact check in docs/hobbies.md, as the October 2026 one was.

## Galleries, catches and maps

- Gallery: full-size files in `staging/hobby-<slug>/`, then `AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT=<account> node scripts/upload-hobby-media.mjs <slug> --hero <file>`, which writes the `media` block. Add captions (otherwise the link reads "Open full-resolution photo"), commit and push. Full-size links work once the next build publishes `incoming/` to `hobby-media/` with GPS stripped.
- Catches: add the entry to `fishing-catches.json`, put the original in the main checkout's `staging/fishing/` (check it decodes, photo-sessions lesson 11), run `node scripts/upload-fishing-catches.mjs`, and commit the JSON with its copy in `src/assets/hobbies/fishing/`. He names staged catches `<species>-<wa|mn>-<place>` so each can be matched to its water (2026-06-28). A hidden spot's name stays out of the published `photo` name and the copy. Catches are split into Washington and Minnesota, open in the lightbox and keep the species sprite above the photo, and a species without a sprite gets one, on the map too ("make one and upadte the maps with it too").
- Map data: `npm run build:herp-geo`, `node scripts/build-fishing-geo.mjs`. Each downloads its source into `.cache/` once.

## Rename a hobby or its URL

Day list became Narrow nature in two commits: the title and copy first (`dfca9e4`), then the slug (`a9c0572`). A slug move touches the JSON (`git mv`), the plates and the `subjects.json` key, the `HobbyBand` `VERBS` key, the `SCENES` key in `src/lib/scenes/table.ts` and its special case in `scenes.test.ts`, doc anchors, and two 301 routes in `staticwebapp.config.json` (the old path and the old path with `/*`). Keep code names, `data-*` hooks and localStorage keys as they are, so saved progress survives. Link `/hobbies/` with its trailing slash. Redirects only work in production (`npm run preview` ignores the SWA config), so check with `curl -I` after the deploy.

## Checks

`npx vitest run src/lib/hobbies src/lib/plates.test.ts`, then `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run check`. Look at the page at 390×844 and 1440×900 in both themes, with the keyboard, and with reduced motion. Judge animation on `npm run build && npm run preview`, not the dev server.

## Truman's verdicts

- Cards: "a logo for each... not clearly AI generated" (2026-10-06); "the logos are really not good... your own created ones are bad" (2026-10-07). Stipple plates from his own photos stuck: "these are great, im impressed" (2026-10-11).
- Home page: "the hobby section to show up a bit more visible and definitily in mobile view as well" (2026-10-06). The `HobbyBand` stays visible on phones.
- Cards say they can be played. A visitor found "it is unclear that you should click on each hobby to go in and play the game" (2026-06-24), so each card ends in an action verb and an arrow (`VERBS` in `HobbyBand.astro`, "Try it" by default). Keep one through any redesign.
- Birding: "(persons face plus some minor bird aspects) and not the other way around"; "needs to look realisitic... not some cartoon" (2026-06-27). No cloud model (2026-06-28). "split the full list into families" (2026-06-29); "show my inaturalist pics... not just generic" (2026-06-30); the life list needed bigger photos on phones, plus search and sort (2026-07-01).
- Herping: "find amphibians in the dark... mainly only salamanders"; "eyeshine glint is a great idea"; "more salamander focused"; "why the flat squares of light and why do eyes completely dissapear in the light"; extend the map to other countries (all 2026-07-08). Faster road finds, and pinch zoom on phones (2026-07-09).
- Aquarium, the first version: "make it more pixel theme"; "get rid of these round green blobs. keep the longer trand ones and maybe add a rock or two" (2026-06-23); "gourami looks nothing similar"; "angelfish doesnt look right, why is it an oval... they don't need to look so cartoonish" (2026-06-24). Each species has its real outline, drawn flat like the fishing sprites. The tank size slider "should stay the same (full width on mobile, etc), but lets have the size of the fish and plants change (more plants if larger size, fish get smaller if larger size)" (2026-06-24, `fishScale` in `aquarium.ts`).
- Aquarium: a new fish "flies and transforms from the color sprite to the actual fish and jumps into the tank, with water droplets... if they spam, it should just have multiple jump in"; clearing the tank should "tip the tank over" (2026-10-14). For the video of his tank he picked a muted hero that starts at the time of day and "seen in my tank" links from the fish, and turned down self-hosting the footage: "can't use just embed youtube somehow" (2026-10-25).
- Fishing maps: "make sure the size of the lakers, their locations, and the size of the rivers and location is correct... the river goes outside of MN which isn't right"; no state border "going up right against the preview frame"; "focus a bit more on near minneapolis but keep lake of the woods and superior for sure... that is where the majority of my catches are"; Washington "mainly more rivers and streams with a tiny bit of the sound area"; "it should show both on the screen at once (for desktop at least). for mobile maybe only show one with clear tab" (2026-06-24).

The beach should "look like a real pnw low tide environment", with mossy rocks and sand that isn't one colour (2026-06-23).
- Hiking trail studio, five rounds in two days: the peaks "look like hills"; "needs way more variety. everything right now is 2 peaks the exact same layout"; "the trail moment sdont do anything at all"; "the route length should scale the size of the mountains"; "it needs more than 5 points you can adjust"; "postcard should be MUCH more detailed" (2026-07-20). Lakes and snow "need to be blended into dips", "mountains aren't entirely green... rock, grass, trees", and then "forest and alpine lake are MUCH better" (2026-07-21, `1044f63`).

The ink heat map that replaced the stipple: "good enough for now... we can improve for future" (2026-11-12).

## Hard-won lessons

1. **Start with a real map.** The herp map was redone five times: a tile-grid choropleth he rejected, a heatmap on real geometry (`f777a73`), world and country views (`a47efc0`), zoom (`0e84ef4`), a 0.1° grid with town names for privacy (`79259d2`) and a CPU readback (`8492c7d`).
2. **Phones need their own map controls.** Clusters were unreadable until a zoom and pan layer with pinch, wheel and buttons, rendering throttled through rAF, and `touch-action: pan-y` that switches to `none` once zoomed (`0e84ef4`).
3. **Open on `click`, never `pointerdown`.** On phones the click from the same tap landed on the new scrim and closed the card it had just opened (`2124ef8`).
4. **Preload reveal photos at a sensible size.** Reveals were slow until species photos preloaded on `requestIdleCallback` at iNaturalist's `medium` (about 120 KB instead of 490 KB) (`be4b54e`).
5. **Full-size catches live in Blob.** Committed 1600 px copies capped the lightbox (`6657e80`), and hidden fishing spots came out of file names and URLs too (`eeaaf9c`).
6. **Birding was redone nine times in two days** (`5aa02e6` to `3dfcbe8`): pixel mascot, person first, bird first, species, photo hybrid, mesh warp. What decided it was the constraint, not the look: on device, no generative model, the selfie never leaves the phone.
7. **Card art took three tries:** emoji, then generated logos he rejected, then stipple plates from his own photos. Never hand-draw icons.
8. **The first-find stamp went across the picture** (`df1b5d7`) until it got its own grid row beside it (`bd89c84`).
9. **Herping eyeshine was backwards.** It vanished when the light hit the animal, and the beam was drawn as flat trapezoids. Eyeshine is brightest when lit, with a radial beam (`f777a73`).
10. **Facts read like AI and some were wrong** (the leather star and swimming anemone mix-up, a chorus frog's colour change taking weeks, a rubber boa's lifespan). A copy pass and a second fact check fixed them, and `species-facts.test.ts` checks the mechanics (`e705d25`).
11. **Copy piled up around a toy as it was rebuilt.** Birding was redone nine times, and each rebuild added a line under the toy without removing the old intro, so the page described a "pixel bird" and a face-morph "bird-person" one above the other and promised privacy three times, once as "the site owner". When a toy changes, rewrite the intro and delete what it replaces. Say privacy once, where the visitor decides (2026-11-09). Text fetched live (Wikipedia summaries) needs the same read as written copy: a summary's first line is usually filler.
12. **The hiking studio was one template in different colours** (2026-07-20). It had five fixed terrain anchors, a distance slider that only changed the stats, a fixed relief, and lakes, snow and trees drawn as ellipses on top. Mileage now sets one to seven mountains and zooms the whole world (change the drag inverse with it), moments carve and sample the terrain, and the editor and postcard share one renderer at different densities (`8cb116b`, `2a71460`, `68c1b87`, `777b2b8`, `1044f63`).
13. **Restyling the frame left the canvas behind.** 2124ef8 (2026-10-12) put the hobby pages in ink on paper but didn't touch what the canvases draw, so the fishing maps' pale ground, the herp map's navy dashboard and bold system-font labels lasted into November. A restyle covers what the canvas draws, and its screenshots include dark mode (2026-11-12).
14. **Stipple dots read as sightings.** The review's mock drew the herp map's heat as stipple, ink dots scattered round each find, and once ported they looked like animals in spots where he'd seen nothing (2026-11-12). On a map, a dot means a find. Density is a heat map in flat tints of ink, darker where finds stack up, with hard edges so it doesn't glow in dark mode (`heatBands`), and only each find's own mark is a dot.
15. **The life list stopped at 200 of 242 species.** `species_counts` was asked for one page of 200, so the heading said 200 and the rarest bird he's logged, a Giant babax with about 35 records worldwide, never reached Rarest sightings (the November 2026 review, TTT-19). Page every iNaturalist list until `total_results`, counting what each page actually returned, and test it past one page (`birding-inat.test.ts`).
16. **A list written into the page has to stay cheap to lay out.** With all 242 rows in the HTML, every font swap laid out about 5,000 boxes, up to 230 ms a pass on a phone at 4x CPU (2026-11-12). Each row's link has `content-visibility: auto` with its exact 81 px height, so rows off screen skip layout until they're near. It's on the link, not the `<li>`, because paint containment would clip the link's focus ring.

## Gotchas

- Islands use a processed `<script>`; `is:inline` would need a CSP hash. DOM built at runtime needs a namespaced `<style is:global>` (`dl-`, `[data-pixel-hike]`), because scoped styles don't reach it.
- Tailwind's Preflight is off, so `[hidden]` loses to a `display` class. Add a scoped `[hidden] { display: none !important }` (`b01e3fa`).
- A literal `<script>` inside an `.astro` comment broke Vite's dev scanner (`f219864`).
- The SpecimenCard photo isn't lazy on purpose: a hidden lazy image is never fetched.
- Every new motion needs a reduced-motion path: stamps, jumps, nets and the tank tip all settle at once.
- `[slug].astro` must keep calling `settleDots()`, or a page reached through a scene stays covered for up to 8 seconds.
- `npm run check` needs at least one session JSON; CI runs `node scripts/generate-fixtures.mjs` first.
- The dev server uses `trailingSlash: 'always'`, so `/hobbies` without the slash 404s there. Restart it after changing `tailwind.config.mjs` or the content schema.
- A key the content schema doesn't declare is dropped without an error. When a bulk revert took `dayList` out of `src/content.config.ts`, the puzzle vanished from the page with nothing in the build log (2026-10-09). If a hobby JSON block stops rendering, check the schema first.
- Headless Chromium blocks iNaturalist photos (`ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB`) and reports the page hidden, so lazy iNaturalist grids stay empty in tests while real browsers load them (2026-06-23). Check in a real browser before "fixing" one.
- Trails I've walked shows each session's cover, never its header: many headers are an animal (a marmot, an ice crawler, a crab), which the review's mock would have put on the trail cards. Name a `photo` when a cover isn't a trail or mountain shot. A renamed or split session drops off the list, with one warning in the build log, until its slug in `trails` is changed too (2026-11-12).

Add new verdicts and lessons here, dated, in the commit that acts on them.
